findings.title: queued defaults to the module-import time, not the instance creation time
findings.body: In the new AssignmentSource dataclass, the field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` exactly once, when the class body is executed at module import. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (including all instances made via `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` in the inbound webhook path) will therefore carry the worker process's import/boot timestamp rather than the time the assignment was actually queued. This value is serialized into every `sync_assignee_outbound` Celery message via `to_dict()`. The field is not consumed by any logic in this PR, so the impact is latent today, but the field's name and inclusion make it clear it is meant to record when the assignment was queued (e.g., for future staleness/ordering checks), and any such use would silently read a wildly stale timestamp. The test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it cannot catch this. Fix: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from `dataclasses`.

findings.title: No test covers outbound propagation to other integrations when a source is set
findings.body: The new cycle-breaking logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` has two contractual halves: (1) suppress the outbound sync back to the integration that originated the assignment, and (2) still propagate the change to other linked integrations — the code comment explicitly promises "This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward." Only half (1) is tested: `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` links a single integration and asserts `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called. There is no test with a second linked integration (e.g., a different integration id) asserting that its outbound sync still fires when `assignment_source` is set, and no test for the deassign path with a matching source. A regression that suppresses all outbound syncs whenever a source is present (e.g., changing the check to `if sync_source: return False`) would pass the entire suite while silently breaking assignee propagation for multi-integration setups, and the inbound-webhook-to-outbound-suppression path via `sync_group_assignee_inbound` is likewise unexercised end to end.
